mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average indicates robust consumer spending that directly supports corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it triggers the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% and rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% signals a tight labor market with aggressive monetary tightening, increasing recession risks and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with monetary tightening
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0 and FEDFUNDS > 2.5, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average indicates manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate capital expenditure and earnings growth, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below its 6-month moving average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2.5% consistently indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 indicate strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 200000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.3 million units and decline in real GDP (GDPC1) below its 4-quarter moving average signals a housing boom in an economic slowdown, increasing recession fears and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1300 and GDPC1 < 4-quarter moving average, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions with real personal consumption (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average and housing starts (HOUST) above 1.2 million, overvaluation and impending monetary tightening cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 12-month MA and HOUST > 1200, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
